Absolutely!

 couple it with your intuition! My apologies if I sound cynical

Characteristics of Capitalism

Throughout its history, but especially during its ascendency in the 19th
 century, capitalism has had certain key characteristics. First, basic
production facilities—land and capital—are privately owned. Capital in
this sense means the buildings, mach ines, and other equipment used to
produce goods and services that are ultimately consumed. Second,
economic activity is organized and coordinated through the interaction
of buyers and sellers (or producers) in markets. Third, owners of land
and capit al as well as the workers they employ are free to pursue their
 own self-interests in seeking maximum gain from the use of their
resources and labor in production. Consumers are free to spend their
incomes in ways that they believe will yield the grea test satisfaction.
 This principle, called consumer sovereignty, reflects the idea that
under capitalism producers will be forced by competition to use their
resources in ways that will best satisfy the wants of consumers.
Self-interest and the pursuit of gain lead them to do this. Fourth,
under this system a minimum of government supervision is required; if
competition is present, economic activity will be self- regulating.
Government will be necessary only to protect society from foreign
attack, uphold the rights of private property, and guarantee contracts.
This 19th-century view of government’s role in the capitalist system has
 been significantly modified by ideas and events of the 20th century.

Deep Blue, your arguments seem to be coming straight from wikipedia; the most reliable source of misinformation there is!

Capitalism and communism, as we’ve seen them, are not opposites. They’re
 just two toes in the same boot which tramples the people. They both
siphon wealth and power from the masses to the very few.

Yes, we’ve allowed tyranny and oppression to be an hallmark of this
society. The greatest weapon invented to perpetuate these evils is
money.

Literally, money = debt. Debt = control. So money = control.

I don’t do pattern recognition. I read the manipulation of the masses by the few.

This, along with years of intensive autodidactic study on how our
society is controlled, actually gives me a reliable view of what’s going
 on, thanks very much.

About Brexit:

People are slowly but surely beginning to realise that our society is
rotten at its core. How many millions of tons of fish must be thrown
overboard, how many millions of unstraight cucumbers must be dumped,
before the people realise they’re living in a farce?

How many top secret “trade agreements” must be foisted upon us, taking
our rights from us and destroying our planet, before we realise that if
we don’t hit the reset button soon we’ll all be living in a wasteland?

This empire has, like every other empire before it which got too big,
begun to crumble under its own weight and hubris. We understand now,
that either it falls, or we fall.

Now, how about you quit the insults, and keep the term “conspiracy theorist” to yourself?

It makes you, rather than me, look stupid!

It’s like the word “heretic” of old. Anybody who refused to believe in
the myriad of imaginary deities floating around in the atmosphere was
ostracised and discredited by the lazy application of a word.

Should I call you a “coincidence theorist” and draw a picture of you
with your head in the sand, or can we have a respectful discussion?

So, you brought up instances in the market where lots of money was lost.
 For every buy there’s a sale, and vice versa. You say lots of money was
 lost. I say lots of money was won! Follow the money and you’ll see
who’s in control.

Your cut and paste Wikipedia definition of capitalism is so far from the truth it’s shocking!

The freedom you talk about is an illusion. Who’s free who has to work
their ass off for thirty years to finally own their own home?

Who’s free that gets most of what they earn taken off them in taxes,
collected to pay off national debts which their governments signed them
up to so the people who created the money from thin air could give
themselves said money to build their empires to the detriment of the
environment and the people?

Who’s free that must keep buying the same essentials over and over,
because said essentials are designed to break soon after buying?

Who’s free that’s forced into poverty unless he joins the army and gets sent abroad to murder his way around the globe?

Who’s free that have their government sign trade deals that allow
corporations to sue the population for loss of earnings should the
country’s policies conflict with the corporation’s plans to control the
market?

Capitalism is not freedom. Capitalism is debt slavery. Capitalism is corporatocracy

Now, onto your second post, and there you are, quoting Wikipedia!!!!

Our masters don’t want money! They want stuff!!!

They create money, out of thin air, every time a loan is made or a credit card is used.

They charge interest on this newly created money, but they don’t create
the money to pay for the interest. This means that the debts can never
be repaid. So, foreclosure is built into the very fabric of the economy.

It’s this foreclosure that our masters want. It allows them to print
money out of nothing and get lots and lots of stuff in return.

Of course, I didn’t go to Yale to learn this stuff, so maybe I’m too stupid to understand it!
